structure: raw-2D self-slicing (identity transform_to_nki_inputs); M-outer; per-M-tile residual add a=x+z; fused SBUF RMSNorm (square -> single full-1024 free-axis reduce -> mean_eps = sumsq*(1/K)+eps via two-op tensor_scalar -> rsqrt); inline per-row [128,1] inv_rms tensor_scalar; inline per-K g multiply (g [1,K].broadcast_to([128,K])); identity nc_matmul transpose of 8 [128,128] K-sub-tiles -> [k_in,m_in]; all-w-resident (8 tiles [128,2048], 64KB/part) loaded once before M-loop; K-accumulate 8 tiles into [128,512] fp32 PSUM; stream 4 N-chunks
eps_form: SAFE: mean_eps = sumsq*(1/K) + eps (two-op tensor_scalar, eps added AFTER /K mean, matches reference exactly); NOT rsqrt((sumsq+eps)/K)
g_placement: inline on activation before matmul (g is per-contraction-column, does NOT commute past GEMM); g-into-w fold deferred to Phase 2
notes: First correct Phase-1 kernel. fp32 throughout, full 5-seed L2 PASS (rel-L2 1.46e-5, ~1.37x under the 2e-5 gate), 3.754x over the 1.859ms baseline. The dominant win is w-residency: HBMrd 42MB (single pass over w+x+z) vs the baseline's ~256MB of in-loop w reloads. PE-bound at the fp32 systolic floor (PE=94% MFU=44%, matching sibling rmsnorm_matmul_v1 97%/46%); RMSNorm cheap/overlapped (Vec 19% Scl 14% DMA 24%). Phase-2 openers: fold g into resident w (8x [128,1] load-time scale vs 32x [128,K] activation multiply) + inv_rms post-scale eviction. Phase-3: compensated bf16x2 split (needs offline multi-draw sim; note the fp32 margin here is only ~1.37x, tighter than the sibling's headroom).

note_type: zero-remote-spend numpy pre-check gating the Phase-2 compensated bf16x2 split
notes: Idealized 3-product bf16x2 (exact fp32 accumulation, numpy RNE limbs) reproduces the EXACT scored input (seed 42 draw x->w->z->g; eps=1e-5 no-draw) and NKIBench reference. Worst rel-L2 4.451e-6 across 7 distinct draws AND both g placements = ~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate and ~3.3x BELOW even the on-device fp32 v1's own 1.46e-5. g-into-w (4.440e-6) marginally MORE accurate than g-on-activation (4.451e-6) and is the cheaper resident-weight fold -> chosen placement. 4-product (keeps lo*lo) = 3.483e-6 held as accuracy-repair fallback. This is the sibling rmsnorm_matmul's proven Phase-3 lever (+28%, 1.066x->1.363x) transferred; authorizes ONE remote bf16x2 attempt in the loop. Idealized: exact fp32 numpy accumulation is >= as accurate as HW, so a fail here would mean HW almost-certainly fails; a pass is a no-spend green light, not a HW guarantee -> full-5-seed remote run still gates promotion.

structure: pure-fp32 refactor of v1: (1) g-into-w' fold -- w'[kt]=tensor_scalar(w_sb[kt], multiply, g_col[kt]) with g_col a [128,1] partition slice of g over the k_in axis, applied 8x at load, leaving w' resident (64KB/part) in place of w; (2) inv_rms post-scale eviction -- out_sb=tensor_scalar(acc, multiply, inv_rms[128,1]) reading the PSUM accumulator directly, replacing v1's nl.copy. RAW a=x+z transposed via identity nc_matmul; fp32 RMSNorm (square/reduce/mean_eps/rsqrt); M-outer; K-accum [128,512] fp32 PSUM over 4 N-chunks
eps_form: SAFE two-op mean_eps = sumsq*(1/K) + eps (eps AFTER /K mean, matches reference); NOT rsqrt((sumsq+eps)/K)
g_placement: folded into resident w' = g*w on the k_in/partition axis (g is per-contraction-column; the fold is the algebraically-correct placement, NOT a free-axis broadcast)
commutations: g-into-w' and inv_rms-post-scale are algebraically-equivalent regroupings of v1; offline fp32_control using exactly these matched the reference to 4.82e-7
promotion: NOT promoted as the phase headline (v3 is the intended promotion), but v2 beats v1 out-of-noise (-3.6%) and is RETAINED (DEC-1) as the pure-fp32 fallback + same-session control + clean base for the v3 bf16 diff
notes: Clean fp32 refactor. Full 5-seed PASS, rel-L2 1.4635e-5 identical to v1 (delta 0.0, << AC-1 +5e-6 margin). Removed v1's two full-width [128,1024] per-M-tile activation passes (inline inv_rms scale + inline g broadcast): g now an 8x load-time [128,1] fold into w', inv_rms now a [128,512]x4 post-scale at eviction -> Vec 19->11%, Scl 14->18%, PE 94->97%, MFU 44->46%. HBM unchanged (42/34MB). The -3.6% is real (v2 stable 0.4770/0.4772/0.4773 vs same-session v1 0.4948) and larger than the sibling v2_postscale's +0.38% precisely because this op's v1 had more inline activation work to shed. This is the base v3 splits into bf16 limbs.
latency_scope: profiler benchmarks ONE kernel per request and reports aggregate LatencyStats (ProfileResult.latency: min/mean/p50/p90/p99/raw_latencies_ms over iters); the per-seed CorrectnessResult carries NO latency field, so per-seed latency is architecturally unavailable. The adapter also reuses the seed-42 input for all 5 profiler seeds, so the timed kernel is identical across seeds and a distinct per-seed latency is not a meaningful quantity here. AC-3 basis = the aggregate p50 over repeated full-5-seed runs (latency_runs_ms), NOT per-seed latency.

split_order: PINNED: weights w'=g*w (fp32 FIRST) -> w'_hi=bf16(w') -> w'_res=w'-w'_hi (fp32 tensor_tensor) -> w'_lo=bf16(w'_res), split ONCE before the M-loop; activation aT=transpose(a) (exact fp32 identity nc_matmul) -> aT_hi=bf16(aT) -> aT_res=aT-aT_hi -> aT_lo=bf16(aT_res), split per transposed sub-tile
products: 3-product: aT_hi@w'_hi + aT_hi@w'_lo + aT_lo@w'_hi in fp32 PSUM (aT_lo@w'_lo DROPPED)
eps_form: SAFE two-op mean_eps = sumsq*(1/K) + eps (eps AFTER /K mean)
g_placement: folded into w' = g*w on the k_in/partition axis, in fp32, BEFORE the bf16 split (matches offline-gated bf16x2_g_into_w)
invariants: fp32 RMSNorm reduction (square/reduce/mean_eps/rsqrt); inv_rms post-scale at PSUM->SBUF eviction; raw-2D I/O + exact signature kernel(x_tensor,w_tensor,eps,z_tensor,g_tensor)
hbm_vs_v1: UNCHANGED (v1 42/34 MB; limbs built on-chip from same fp32 HBM loads, no spill)
promotion: PROMOTED -- clears BOTH gates: full-5-seed l2_norm_passed=True (rel-L2 1.528e-5, 1.31x under gate) AND -18.9% out-of-noise latency win over same-session v1 (>> 1.8% band), repeated 2x full-5-seed with <0.03% jitter. Breaks the fp32 PE floor (3.754x -> 4.632x)
rel_l2_quadrature: on-device 1.528e-5 = sqrt(fp32-floor 1.4635e-5^2 + bf16 4.38e-6^2); the 4.38e-6 delta == offline bf16x2 error 4.45e-6 -> bf16 arithmetic behaves exactly as predicted; the excess over the idealized 4.45e-6 is the pre-existing HARDWARE fp32 floor (also in v1/v2), not a v3 defect. Confirmed by the D3 4-product measurement (removing the dropped term barely moves rel-L2)
notes: The intended Phase-2 promotion. Transfers the sibling rmsnorm_matmul_v4's proven compensated bf16x2 lever (there -21.8%, 1.363x). Here -18.9% (slightly less extreme; PE 89% vs sibling 96% -> more residual PE headroom from this op's extra per-M-tile overhead: residual add a=x+z and the g-into-w' fold). HBMrd 42MB (vs sibling 25MB) from the extra z read lifts DMA to 29%, still hidden under PE. v1 (3.754x) and v2 (fp32 refactor, 3.898x) retained as pure-fp32 fallbacks (DEC-1) against the fixed-seed-42 adapter input-diversity caveat.

products: 4-product: aT_hi@w'_hi + aT_hi@w'_lo + aT_lo@w'_hi + aT_lo@w'_lo in fp32 PSUM (keeps the term v3 drops; 32 vs 24 matmuls per N-chunk)
trigger: v3 on-device rel-L2 1.528e-5 crossed the plan's >~1.5e-5 D3 marginal trigger (AC-6), so D3 was measured (not proactively explored)
decision: REJECT. The 4th product improves rel-L2 only 1.528e-5 -> 1.503e-5 (~1.6%, exactly the quadrature prediction sqrt(1.4635^2 + 3.48^2)=1.504e-5) but REGRESSES latency +28% (0.4013 -> 0.5145), dropping speedup 4.632x -> 3.614x (below even v1's 3.754x). v3 already passes at 1.31x margin, so the negligible accuracy gain is not worth un-promoting. The rel-L2 'excess' over the offline 4.45e-6 is the fp32 HARDWARE floor (unfixable by more bf16 cross terms), which D3 confirms: adding lo*lo leaves rel-L2 pinned near the fp32-floor 1.46-1.50e-5.
notes: First-class negative datum that validates v3's 3-product choice. Kept in runs/ as tracked evidence, NOT promoted. Closes the D3 direction with a measurement rather than the model alone.

bit_exact_vs_v3: BIT-EXACT: per-seed rel-L2 == v3's 1.528161e-5 on all 5 seeds, |delta|=0 <= the 1e-7 AC-3 tolerance. An exact fp32 SBUF copy of psum_t is bit-identical to psum_t itself, so bf16(psum_t) and (psum_t - aT_hi) reproduce EXACTLY the two bf16 limbs v3 consumes; the 3-product matmul is byte-for-byte v3.
lever: D1 -- split the transposed activation limbs DIRECTLY from the transpose PSUM bank (psum_t): drop v3's intermediate fp32 SBUF copy aT_f; aT_hi=bf16(psum_t), aT_res=psum_t-aT_hi (fp32 tensor_tensor, PSUM-space first operand), aT_lo=bf16(aT_res). 4->3 ops per K-sub-tile (32->24 Vec/Scalar ops per M-tile in the SOURCE).
compile_semantic_gate: status=success -- CODEGEN-FEASIBLE; no PSUM-bank/spill/allocation error. Reading ONE operand from PSUM is proven (the inv_rms post-scale reads the accumulator); the second tensor_tensor operand stays SBUF, so both-operands-in-PSUM is NOT triggered. --fast rel-L2 1.528161e-5 == v3 (gate passed before any full-5-seed/profiling spend, AC-2).
compiled_artifact_vs_v3: IDENTICAL compiled kernel: Vec instr 314==314, Scl instr 376==376, matmul instr 3336==3336, HBMrd 42013184==42013184 B, HBMwr 33554432==33554432 B, spill_reload 0/0, spill_save 0/0, PE_active_ns 716061 vs 714234 (-0.26%). The trn2 compiler (neuronx-cc) already copy-propagated v3's exact aT_f fp32 PSUM->SBUF copy into the downstream cast+subtract -- i.e. it had ALREADY applied D1 at lowering, so the removed SOURCE ops carried no distinct hardware work.
promotion: NOT promoted. AC-5 gate: full-5-seed PASS (yes, bit-exact) AND p50 >1.8% out of noise vs a same-session v3 anchor (NO: +0.09%, inside the 0.4005-0.4017 v3 band, stable p90). -> WITHIN-NOISE FLOOR-CONFIRMATION; v3 stays promoted at 4.632x. v4 kept as tracked evidence: a cleaner, bit-exact source expression of v3 that the compiler lowers to the same artifact.
d2_gate: D2/v5 (AC-9) NOT triggered: the digest shows NO measurable Vec/Scalar bubble (Vec 22% / Scl 24% unchanged from v3, identical instr counts, both hidden under PE 89%). Building v5 would be a forbidden proactive D2. Skipped by measurement.
notes: Phase-3 primary lever D1. Bit-exact by construction and confirmed on hardware (rel-L2 1.528161e-5, |delta vs v3|=0). The op-specific PE-idle gap (v3 PE=89% vs sibling 96%) is the residual add a=x+z + z-read + fp32 RMSNorm reduction; the digest shows these are HIDDEN under the PE-bound 3-product matmul, not exposed, so removing the redundant aT_f copy (which the compiler had already elided) does not move the wall clock. Mirrors the sibling rmsnorm_matmul phase-3 finding that transpose/stationary-fills were already hidden at PE=96%. HBM 42/34MB unchanged, no spill. v1 (3.754x) / v2 (3.898x) retained as pure-fp32 fallbacks (AC-8.1).

Fixing the adapter is OUT of scope (NKIBench benchmark contract); this evidence is stated against the current contract. NOT a claim of genuine per-seed input diversity.

direction: D3 (phase-3): split a's limbs as WIDE [128,1024] ops BEFORE transposing (3 wide ops instead of 24 small ones)
closure_rationale: DO NOT IMPLEMENT. Splitting before the transpose DOUBLES the transpose PE work: each of a_hi and a_lo must be transposed separately -> 16 transpose nc_matmuls + 16 PSUM->SBUF copies per M-tile vs v3's 8. That ADDS PE-active (the one thing we cannot afford; PE-active ~355us is the unmovable 3-product floor) to save fixed-overhead Vec ops. Phase-2 already established 'split AFTER the transpose costs ONE transpose, not two'; D1 preserves that single-transpose property while shrinking the source op count. Adding transpose PE to shave already-hidden Vec ops is a guaranteed regression.
notes: Distinct from the phase-2 D3 4-product reject (add_rmsnorm_matmul_v3b_bf16_split4): that was a PRECISION direction (extra product); this D3 is a SCHEDULE direction (limb-split placement relative to the transpose). Both are closed. First-class negative datum per AC-7; not built.

direction: D4: move the [128,128] activation transpose off the Tensor engine (bf16-limb world)
closure_rationale: DO NOT EXPLORE. Re-checked for bf16 tiles (the sibling closed it for fp32): (1) SBUF->SBUF dma_transpose of a [128,128] tile is STILL infeasible -- the hardware-DGE path needs src.shape[0]==16, the software-DGE path needs the source in HBM; the shape/memory constraints block it, not just the dtype. (2) nc_transpose(bf16) lands in fp32 PSUM and needs a re-cast (no net win), and the sibling rmsnorm_matmul MEASURED a vector-engine transpose at +2% (Vec becomes a co-bottleneck). The identity-matmul transpose stays -- it is a near-free [128,128] matmul-against-identity fully HIDDEN under the PE-bound main matmul (v4 digest: the transpose is not on the wall-clock critical path).
notes: First-class negative datum per AC-7; not built (compile-feasibility already known-closed).

direction: D5: change the matmul precision / product count (more or fewer bf16 products)
closure_rationale: FORBIDDEN this phase. The 3-product bf16 arithmetic is PINNED: on-device margin is only 1.31x (rel-L2 1.528e-5 vs the 2e-5 gate), so fewer products / plain bf16 fail (plain single-limb bf16 = 2.345e-3, ~117x over the gate). Going the other way, the 4-product variant is already a MEASURED-REJECT (add_rmsnorm_matmul_v3b_bf16_split4: rel-L2 improves only 1.528e-5->1.503e-5 (~1.6%) but latency REGRESSES +28% to 0.5145ms, 4.632x->3.614x, below even v1). The rel-L2 'excess' over the offline 4.45e-6 is the pre-existing fp32 HARDWARE floor (present in v1/v2 too, quadrature sqrt(1.4635^2+4.4^2)e-6=1.528e-5), unfixable by more bf16 cross terms. Phase 3 optimizes the SCHEDULE around the fixed 3-product arithmetic, not the arithmetic.
notes: First-class negative datum per AC-7; D3-4product measured, plain-bf16 offline-simmed.
